⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🩺 Dr. Siddharth Katkade
Consultant Spine Surgeon
Bombay Spine Clinic™

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

📍 Bombay Spine Clinic
Dr. Siddharth Katkade | Consultant Spine Surgeon

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

Dr. Siddharth Katkade | Consultant Spine Surgeon

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Healthy Hips, Strong Spine

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

✅ Improve posture
✅ Reduce lower back pain
✅ Increase flexibility & mobility
✅ Support spinal alignment

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | The 20-20-20 Eye–Neck Rule

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away
✅ For 20 seconds

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we commonly see patients with office-related neck pain, posture-related spine problems, cervical spondylosis, and work-from-home back pain linked to prolonged screen usage and poor ergonomics.

🩺 SPINE CLINICAL INSIGHT
Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is often missed in routine OPD practice and treated as simple cervical spondylosis.

Early clues include:
✔️ Hand clumsiness
✔️ Gait imbalance or frequent falls
✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign
✔️ Progressive weakness or stiffness
✔️ Bilateral upper limb symptoms

🚨 Red Flags Requiring Urgent Referral:
* Bowel/bladder dysfunction
* Rapidly progressive weakness
* Severe gait instability

📌 MRI Cervical Spine remains the gold standard investigation.

Early diagnosis and timely referral can prevent irreversible neurological decline and improve patient outcomes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
After looking at the 5-star reviews, I visited this doctor for my mother’s left leg pain. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. The doctor is polite in speech but seems very money-minded.

During the first visit, he charged ₹1500 (normal fees), but strongly insisted on getting a Doppler test done through a specific lab. He even called the lab in front of us and mentioned sending the patient directly, which clearly felt like a commission-based referral. This was despite us clearly stating that we wanted to do the test at another known place. He claimed that ultrasounds done elsewhere would not be reliable. The lab he suggested charged ₹6000, while we got the same test done at our known place for ₹5000.

As instructed, we shared the report with him on WhatsApp, but there was no response. Later, my brother personally visited the clinic just to show the reports (the patient was not present). Ideally, this should have been free since it was only for report discussion, but he still charged ₹1000. On top of that, he again recommended another radiologist by sharing a specific name and phone number.

Overall, this was the most money-minded and disappointing experience I’ve had with a doctor.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello! I really feel sorry for patients like you.It is unfortunate that when a correct clinical diagnosis was made and appropriate steps were taken to prevent you from being misled, the response is criticism rather than appreciation. You previously did an incorrect scan elsewhere, which you don't have anything to say about. Now, when a correct scan was suggested after clinical examination, and a correct diagnosis was made, here you are making allegations without even having visited for the follow up consultation and understanding the problem. Let's get the facts clear!

The reason a specific centre was suggested, was to prevent a repeat of an incorrect investigation (like you did before). Prior to consulting me, a venous Doppler had already been done, while your mother’s clinical presentation was not sciatica or venous problem, but strongly suggestive of arterial insufficiency (ischemic pain). A venous Doppler would never diagnose this condition.

The recommendation was therefore for a proper arterial Doppler, done by a senior, reliable radiologist, with whom precise requirements could be clearly communicated. The phone call was made only to ensure the correct study was performed this time — not for any financial reason. I have no commission arrangements, nor do I compel patients to visit any particular center. You were always free to choose where to do the test, which you ultimately did — and the scan confirmed the arterial block, exactly as suspected clinically. (which you should rather appreciate for spot on clinical diagnosis!)

Suggesting accuracy over repetition of wrong tests is called responsible medical practice, not “money-mindedness”.

At no point were you instructed to seek treatment or consultation over WhatsApp. Medical opinions are not given casually over messages.

Your brother later visited the clinic for formal report discussion and guidance, which constitutes a consultation. Doctors do not charge for “presence of the patient” — they charge for professional expertise, time, and responsibility involved in interpreting reports and guiding next steps. This is the same principle by which professionals in any field are paid for their work. Do you or your family members work for free? or ever say to your boss that you don't want payment for a particular month? or a 50% less salary this month would be okay?

If there was any financial difficulty, it could have been communicated. We offer concessions, fee waivers, and charity OPD options for genuinely needy patients. We doctors do that.

It is disappointing that sincere efforts to guide a patient onto the correct diagnostic path are interpreted otherwise. Medicine requires trust in clinical judgment, not assumptions about intent.

I genuinely wish your mother good health. However, when decision-makers are like you who lack trust and respect for sound medical advice, it may indeed be better to continue with whose approach you are more comfortable with and keep on doing investigation after investigations. All the best! 👍🏻

Vitamin B12 deficiency is one of the most common undiagnosed deficiency conditions in today's date.

It occurs when the body does not get enough vitamin B12 through our diet, an essential nutrient for healthy nerves, red blood cells, and DNA production. 

Common symptoms include: 
- fatigue
- generalised weakness 
- numbness or tingling in the hands and feet, 
- memory problems
- irritability
- hair loss

It may result from poor dietary intake, especially in strict vegetarians, or from conditions that reduce absorption, such as certain stomach or intestinal disorders. 

Diagnosis is made through blood tests. Treatment includes dietary changes, oral supplements, or injections depending on the severity.

If you are suffering from any of the above symptoms, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert opinion and complete orthopedic care.

SHOULDER DISLOCATION

A shoulder dislocation occurs when the ball of the upper arm bone comes out of its socket completely. 

It can happen after a fall, road traffic accident or during a contact sport. 

Patients experience sudden onset severe pain, difficulty in moving the arm and a visible deformity around the shoulder. 

Emergency care by an orthopaedic surgeon is required as it must be reduced back into its position.

Once the joint is reduced, proper rehabilitation is essential to restore strength and movement. Most of the patients do well later.

Rarely in cases of repeated dislocations, a key-hole arthroscopic surgery is required to repair the torn tissue.

If you are suffering from repeated dislocations of shoulder, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert advice and complete orthpedic care.

PLANTAR FASCIITIS 

Heel pain is one of the commonest orthopedic complaints faced by millions of people worldwide and plantar fasciitis is the leading cause.

It can affect anyone who needs to stand or walk for long hours at work or for any other reason.

If you are experiencing persistent heel pain, then this blog will answer many of your doubts.

Tennis elbow or Lateral Epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain.

It is caused by overuse of the forearm muscles and hence the tendons that attach on the outer side of the elbow. 

Despite its name, it does not affect only tennis players but it can affect anyone who performs repetitive gripping, lifting, typing, or wrist movements. 

Symptoms include pain and tenderness on the outer elbow, reduced grip strength, and discomfort while lifting objects or shaking hands. 

Most patients improve with activity modification, ice fomentation, anti-inflammatory medications and stretching exercises. 
Rarely PRP injection and surgery are used as the last resorts.

Early treatment helps prevent chronic pain and allows a quicker return to daily activities and sports.

If you are suffering from constant elbow pain, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert orthopedic care.

Jumper’s Knee (Patellar Tendinopathy)

Jumper’s knee is an overuse injury affecting the tendon connecting the knee cap (patella) to the shin bone (tibia). 

It commonly occurs in athletes involved in jumping sports such as basketball, volleyball, and athletics. 

Patients typically experience pain at the front of the knee, especially during jumping, running, squatting, or climbing stairs. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, ice application, and physiotherapy focused on strengthening the quadriceps and tendon. Ignoring symptoms can lead to chronic pain and reduced performance. 

Timely diagnosis and appropriate rehabilitation are essential for a successful recovery.

If you are suffering from similar symptoms, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic advice and care.

Para-Meniscal Cyst of Knee: sign of an underlying meniscus tear

A para-meniscal cyst is a fluid-filled swelling that develops next to the meniscus (C-shaped cushion inside the knee joint)

It usually occurs when joint fluid escapes through a small meniscal tear and collects outside the meniscus. 

Patients notice a localised bump near the knee along with pain, tenderness, and discomfort during activities likje walking, climbing stairs. 

MRI is the best investigation to confirm the diagnosis and identify the associated meniscal tear. 

Treatment depends on severity and duration of symptoms and includes medicines & physiotherapy to arthroscopic (key-hole) surgery to repair the underlying meniscus tear and prevent recurrence of the cyst.

If you are suffering from persistent knee pain or a localised swelling along the knee joint, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic care.

METATARSALGIA : FOREFOOT PAIN

Metatarsalgia is a common condition causing pain and inflammation in the ball of the foot, usually beneath the metatarsal bones. 

It often develops due to excessive walking, running, high-impact sports, improper footwear, foot deformities, or being overweight. 

Patients typically experience a burning, aching, or sharp pain that worsens while standing or walking and improves with rest. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, orthotic insoles, stretching exercises, and anti-inflammatory medications fora short course. 

However identifying and addressing the underlying cause is essential to prevent chronic symptoms and restore comfortable, pain-free mobility.

If you are suffering from pain over the forefoot, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for best orthopedic advice and care!

WRIST SPRAIN is an injury caused by stretching or tearing of the ligaments that support the wrist joint.

It commonly occurs after a fall on an outstretched hand, twisting injury or lifting weights at the gym or during a sport. 

Symptoms include sudden pain, swelling, bruising, tenderness, and difficulty moving the wrist or gripping objects. 

Immediate care includes rest to the joint, ice application, compression with a crepe bandage, elevation, and temporary splint support. 

Persistent pain and/or swelling beyond 1-2 days should not be ignored and needs urgent medical attention.

If you are have sustained a wrist injury, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at Sphere Clinic, Parel East, Mumbai for expert advice and care.

HYALURONIC ACID INJECTION

A major cause of knee pain in old age is knee osteoarthritis, a degenerative condition in which the smooth cartilage lining of the knee gradually wears out. 

While physiotherapy, weight management, and medications help most of the patients, some continue to have persistent symptoms. 

In such cases, hyaluronic acid injections can be considered as a safe and effective non-surgical treatment option.

CALCIUM SUPPLEMENTS IN ELDERLY 

- As we age, calcium absorption through gut reduces, increasing the risk of osteoporosis (weak bones) and fractures. 

- In women, this risk further increases due to hormonal changes.

- Elder individuals benefit from calcium supplements when dietary intake is inadequate. 

- The preferred supplements are calcium citrate and calcium carbonate. 

- Calcium citrate is better absorbed in people with low stomach acid and causes less bloating, making it suitable for older adults. 

- Calcium carbonate is economical and works best when taken with meals. 

- Most elderly patients require 1000–1200 mg of elemental calcium daily along with adequate vitamin D for proper absorption. 

- Although excessive calcium intake is hazardous and should be avoided. It is advisable to take supplements only as per your doctor's advice.

- Remember! Calcium supplements are always complementary to a balanced diet and can not replace it.

Back Pain Should Never Be Ignored – It May Be a Warning Sign of Spine TB

A young patient from Byculla, Mumbai, initially came to me with only back pain. Since there were no major neurological symptoms at first, he was started on medicines and kept under close observation with regular follow-up. For a few weeks he was doing well, but then he stopped coming for follow-up.

After some time, he suddenly called me with imbalance while walking for 5 days and difficulty passing urine. I immediately advised admission. On examination, he had already started developing weakness in both lower limbs. An urgent MRI spine showed spinal TB with epidural collection causing compression of the spinal cord in the lumbar region.

This was a neurosurgical emergency. He was taken up for urgent surgery, the pressure on the spinal cord was relieved, and thankfully he had an excellent post-operative recovery with complete regain of power in both legs.

This case highlights an important message: never ignore persistent back pain, especially if it worsens or is associated with walking imbalance, leg weakness, or urinary difficulty. In conditions like Koch’s spine / spinal TB, delayed treatment can lead to permanent nerve damage or paralysis. Timely diagnosis, regular follow-up, and early surgical intervention when needed can result in full recovery.

If you are suffering from back pain, spine infection, spinal TB, leg weakness, or nerve compression, consult Dr. Bhushan Meshram, Neurosurgeon.

Young Professionals & IT Employees: Don’t Ignore Neck Pain – It May Be a New Occupational Hazard

In today’s digital world, neck pain in the young generation is becoming increasingly common, especially among people working long hours in IT jobs, desk jobs, and computer-based professions. Prolonged sitting, poor posture, continuous laptop use, and lack of movement are turning neck pain into a new occupational hazard.

Common symptoms include neck stiffness, pain radiating to the shoulders or arms, tingling or numbness in the hands, headaches, and even weakness in the arms. If ignored, these problems may lead to cervical disc prolapse, nerve compression, or cervical spondylosis at a young age.

How to prevent neck pain:
✔ Maintain correct sitting posture
✔ Keep your screen at eye level
✔ Use an ergonomic chair and proper back support
✔ Take short breaks every 30–40 minutes
✔ Do regular neck stretching and strengthening exercises
✔ Avoid prolonged mobile/laptop bending posture

When should you see a neurosurgeon?
If your neck pain is persistent, severe, associated with arm pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, imbalance while walking, or is not improving with rest and physiotherapy, timely consultation is important.

Dr. Bhushan Meshram, Neurosurgeon, offers expert evaluation and treatment for neck pain, cervical spine problems, slipped disc, and nerve compression. Early diagnosis can prevent long-term complications.

Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH): A Treatable Cause of Memory Loss and Walking Difficulty

Many elderly patients experience difficulty walking, forgetfulness, and loss of bladder control, often assuming it is a normal part of aging. However, these symptoms may be due to Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH), a condition caused by excess cerebrospinal fluid accumulating in the brain.

The classic symptoms of NPH include:
✔ Difficulty walking or imbalance while walking
✔ Memory problems or confusion
✔ Urinary urgency or loss of bladder control

The good news is that Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus is one of the few reversible causes of dementia-like symptoms. Early diagnosis with brain imaging and proper neurological evaluation can make a significant difference.

If identified and treated in time, many patients can experience remarkable improvement in walking, memory, and daily activities. Treatment usually involves the placement of a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt, which helps drain excess fluid from the brain.

Awareness is crucial. If you or your loved one has developed unexplained gait imbalance, memory decline, or urinary symptoms, do not ignore these warning signs. Timely consultation with an experienced neurosurgeon can help achieve excellent outcomes and even complete recovery in suitable cases.

Dr. Bhushan Meshram, one of the leading neurosurgeons in Mumbai, provides advanced diagnosis and treatment for Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus and other brain disorders.

World Brain Tumor Day: Early Diagnosis Can Save Lives

On World Brain Tumor Day, it is important to spread awareness about brain tumors, their symptoms, and the available treatment options.

A brain tumor is an abnormal growth of cells within the brain. Brain tumors can be benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous). Common types include meningioma, glioma, pituitary tumors, acoustic neuroma, metastatic brain tumors, and pediatric brain tumors.

Symptoms of a Brain Tumor
✔ Persistent headaches, especially in the morning
✔ Seizures or fits
✔ Weakness in the arms or legs
✔ Difficulty in speech or memory
✔ Imbalance while walking
✔ Blurred or double vision
✔ Personality or behavioral changes

Treatment Options
Treatment depends on the type, size, and location of the tumor and may include:
• Advanced microsurgical brain tumor removal
• Endoscopic brain surgery
• Radiation therapy
• Chemotherapy
• Targeted and multidisciplinary treatments

Early diagnosis and timely treatment can significantly improve outcomes and quality of life.

If you or a loved one experiences persistent neurological symptoms, seek expert evaluation.

Neck Pain, Hand Weakness & Imbalance While Walking? It Could Be OPLL (Ossified Posterior Longitudinal Ligament)

A 56-year-old gentleman visited our clinic with severe neck pain radiating to both arms, tingling and numbness in his hands, difficulty holding objects, and increasing imbalance while walking.

On examination, he was found to have cervical myelopathy, a serious condition caused by pressure on the spinal cord. His MRI revealed Ossified Posterior Longitudinal Ligament (OPLL) causing severe cervical spinal cord compression along with myelomalacia (damage to the spinal cord).

Considering the progressive neurological symptoms, he underwent cervical laminectomy with cervical spine fusion surgery. The results were encouraging—his hand grip improved immediately after surgery. With dedicated physiotherapy, his walking balance gradually improved, and within two months he regained independence in his daily activities.

This case highlights the importance of early diagnosis and timely surgical intervention in OPLL and cervical myelopathy. Delaying treatment can lead to permanent nerve damage, severe disability, or even paralysis.

If you are experiencing neck pain, arm numbness, hand weakness, difficulty with fine movements, or imbalance while walking, seek expert evaluation without delay.

Persistent Headache in a Teenager Turned Out to Be Arnold Chiari Malformation

A 15-year-old girl visited my clinic with a history of severe headaches for the last 2 years. The pain typically started at the back of the neck and radiated to the forehead. She had been treated as a migraine patient by multiple doctors, but her symptoms continued.

During a detailed consultation, one symptom stood out—intermittent numbness in her left arm. A thorough neurological examination revealed subtle weakness in her left hand, which she had ignored because she was right-hand dominant. Her reflexes were exaggerated, suggesting an underlying neurological problem. On further questioning, she also reported imbalance while walking, especially on uneven surfaces.

An urgent MRI brain and cervical spine confirmed Arnold Chiari Malformation, a condition where the cerebellar tonsils descend through the foramen magnum, causing compression of the brainstem and spinal cord.

She underwent Foramen Magnum Decompression Surgery the following week and made an excellent recovery, being discharged within 5 days.

This case highlights the importance of meticulous history taking and neurological examination. Not every headache is migraine. Persistent headaches associated with numbness, weakness, balance issues, or neurological symptoms should never be ignored, especially in young adults and children.

Keywords: Arnold Chiari Malformation, Chiari Malformation Surgery, Foramen Magnum Decompression, Chronic Head

Kyphoplasty and Nerve Root Block: Avoiding Major Spine Surgery in Elderly Patients

A 65-year-old lady came to me with severe back and leg pain that had returned just one month after undergoing lumbar fusion surgery (L4-S1) elsewhere. Over the next few months, her symptoms worsened, making walking and daily activities difficult.

After taking a detailed history, performing a thorough neurological examination, and carefully reviewing all her scans, I found that the source of her pain had been missed. Her leg pain was due to compression of the L5 nerve root, while her severe back pain was caused by an osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture that had not been identified during the previous surgery.

Considering her age, diabetes, and hypertension, a major revision spine surgery with a longer fusion would have involved a large incision, prolonged recovery, and higher surgical risks.

Instead, I offered a minimally invasive solution: L5 nerve root block and Kyphoplasty, both performed under local anesthesia through tiny needle punctures without any major cuts.

The procedure was successful. Her back and leg pain improved dramatically, she was able to walk comfortably, and she was discharged the very next day.

This case highlights how Kyphoplasty for osteoporotic spine fractures and targeted nerve root injections can provide excellent pain relief and functional recovery in carefully selected patients, often avoiding the need for extensive revision spine surgery.

Safe Brain Tumor Surgery Near the Motor Cortex with Neuromonitoring

Advanced Neuromonitoring Helps Preserve Brain Function During Brain Tumor Surgery

A 70-year-old gentleman from Lalbaug came to me with gradually worsening weakness of the left hand and leg. His relatives noticed difficulty in walking and reduced strength on the left side, following which an MRI brain scan revealed a large right-sided brain tumor. The tumor was located dangerously close to the motor cortex — the vital area of the brain that controls body movements.

I explained to the family that surgery was necessary, but because the tumor was very close to the nerve fibres controlling movement, there was a significant risk of paralysis. To improve safety, we planned the surgery with advanced intraoperative neuromonitoring.

Neuromonitoring during brain tumor surgery helps identify and protect critical brain pathways in real time. It allows precise tumor excision while preserving important neurological function and minimizing the risk of permanent weakness or paralysis.

The surgery lasted nearly 4 hours. The patient stayed in the ICU for one day and recovered remarkably well. The brain tumor was completely excised, and most importantly, he had no paralysis after surgery.

Modern neurosurgery is not just about removing a tumor — it is about preserving quality of life. Neuromonitoring plays a crucial role in safe brain tumor surgery and protection of vital brain function

Severe Back Pain After a Minor Fall? Osteoporotic Spine Fracture Treated Without Major Surgery

An elderly lady from Rasayani/Panvel (Navi Mumbai) with multiple medical problems visited me with severe back pain and inability to sit, stand, or walk. She had suffered a trivial fall a month earlier and had been on medications and conservative treatment since then, but her pain continued to worsen.

On examination and imaging, she was diagnosed with an osteoporotic compression fracture of the spine—a common yet often disabling condition in elderly patients with weak bones.

Considering her age and comorbidities, I discussed the option of vertebroplasty, a minimally invasive spine procedure where medical cement is injected into the fractured vertebra to stabilize the bone and relieve pain. I explained that the procedure could be performed under awake local anesthesia, avoiding the risks of major surgery.

She underwent vertebroplasty and the transformation was remarkable. By the same evening, she was able to walk pain-free. The relief on her face and happiness of her family reminded us how timely treatment can restore independence and quality of life.

Persistent back pain after a minor fall should never be ignored. Early diagnosis and treatment can make all the difference.
